💡 Key Takeaways
  • With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant.
  • The move, which has yet to be publicly announced by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play.
  • The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With just weeks to go until the start of the 2027 World Junior Championship, it remains unclear who will be the 10th, and final, participant. This comes after the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association mentioned the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) had said it had been removed from the tournament so that Russia could take part.

The move, which has yet to be publicly announced by the IIHF, comes in apparent response to the Court of Arbitration (CAS) ruling in late October, which ordered it to allow Russia to return to international play. The World Juniors is the first tournament affected by the CAS decision.

The IIHF barred Russia and Belarus from international play shortly after Moscow released its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

In a statement issued Saturday, the IIHF noted it was "taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization's financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey.".

It has been revealed that as of Monday, the IIHF website still listed Norway as one of the participants in the World Juniors, which is to be hosted by Edmonton and Red Deer, Alberta, beginning on December 26. But Swiss Ice Hockey has responded to Norway's statement, saying its team would not face Russia at the World Juniors — as would be the case if it replaces Norway in the schedule.

However, it's far from certain that Russia will actually be able to ice a team in the tournament, as just last week, the Canadian prime minister ruled out the possibility.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," remarked Mark Carney.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

According to recent reports, how this circle could be squared is unclear. Carney's pledge, coupled with the stated refusal by Finland, Sweden, Switzerland and others to face Russia in an international tournament, appears to have given the Norwegian Ice Hockey Association (NIHF) hope that its team could still play in the upcoming tournament. Several long-time corporate sponsors have also threatened to pull out if Russia is allowed to compete.

"This makes us hope that the last word has not been said about our participation in Canada in December," said NIHF General Secretary Petter Salsten.

"The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association is awaiting further information from the IIHF in the coming days.".

Meanwhile, the German Ice Hockey Association (DEB) is still in discussions with the government in Berlin and the IIHF about how to proceed — or not — with hosting the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in May.

"We intend to host the world championship in Germany next year, and I am very optimistic that we will succeed in doing so," DEB chairman Frank H. Lutz told German broadcaster MagentaSport on Saturday.

While he acknowledged the IIHF's CAS-ordered requirement to include Russia and reiterated the DEB's rejection of the court ruling, he provided no indication as to how this obstacle could be overcome.

Lutz, who remarked he would be in Berlin for more consultations this week, had previously said handing back Germany's hosting rights was a possibility — if only as a last resort.

On Friday, government spokesman Stefan Kornelius remarked Berlin supports the DEB's efforts to find a solution.

"However, given the boycotts that would follow Russia's readmission, that would effectively be impossible. For this reason, we intend to explore, through dialogue, how we can still ensure the tournament takes place.".

Asked at the same press conference whether Germany could glitch visas to a Russian team for the tournament, a Foreign Ministry spokesman indicated that this would be difficult under restrictions currently in place.

"At a time when Russia is waging a war of aggression against Ukraine, there can be no 'normalcy' — and we will certainly not pretend that there is," said spokesperson Martin Giese.

However, he did not categorically rule out the possibility.

It has been suggested that government officials could be choosing their words carefully out of concern for Munich's chances as it bids to host the Summer Olympics in 2036, 2040 or 2044.

The International Olympic Committee (IOC) recently lifted its sanctions on Russian athletes and suspension of the Russian National Olympic Committee, opening the door for their return to competition despite the ongoing war in Ukraine.

The thinking goes that the IOC would expect national Olympic committees who are bidding to host an Olympic Games — like the German Olympic Sports Confederation (DOSB) — to follow its lead.

Asked whether the debate over Russia's possible involvement in a hockey tournament could affect Munich's chances, government spokesman Kornelius noted he didn't wish to "speculate on implications.".

Still, with the IOC set to decide in the next few weeks whether Munich advances to the next stage of the process, one has to think that the matter could hardly have come up at a more inopportune time for the DOSB.

By Matt Law | 24 Nov 2026 11:51, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 11:52.

Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a contest against Azerbaijani outfit Sabah on Wednesday evening.

The La Liga giants are fifth in the overall table on nine points, while Sabah are 31st, collecting three points from their opening four matches of the 2026-27 league stage.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 5.45pm UK time on Wednesday.

The Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona will be played at Baku Olympic Stadium.

Boasting a seating capacity of just under 70,000, it is the largest stadium in Azerbaijan.

The Champions League match will be shown live on TNT Sports 4.

TNT Sports is also available as an add-on for Amazon's Prime Video app.

Goals will be posted on the FootballOnTNT X account, while highlights will also be uploaded to the TNT Sports Football YouTube channel after the match.

History will be made on Wednesday, as Sabah and Barcelona prepare to lock horns for the first time, and the hosts will be eyeing a stunning win over the La Liga champions.

Sabah have won one and lost three of their matches in the league stage of the competition, while Barcelona have a record of three wins and one defeat.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, and they will now be taking on one of the biggest club teams in European football.

Barcelona lost in the last-16 stage of last season's Champions League to Atletico Madrid, so there is clear room for improvement during the current campaign.

Sabah are the huge underdogs entering this match, but the fact that Lamine Yamal will not be involved for Barcelona due to an injury will hand the hosts a degree of confidence.

What do various cancers have in common?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
  • Get Nature+, our best-value online-access subscription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

What Martin O’Neill wouldn’t give to see more of this until the point where the cavalry appears on top of the hill in January.

Celtic wins with bells and whistles attached have been as rare as hen’s teeth since this campaign began.

That the supporters witnessed one in trying circumstances felt significant given the arduous schedule which awaits in the coming six weeks.

According to recent reports, despite having no option but to piece together a midfield, O’Neill watched his side create a slew of opportunities. They took four with as many different scorers and might well have had more.

Sources indicate that A display brimming with enterprise and imagination boded well for what lies ahead. For the first time since September, Celtic have chalked up three straight wins. Ahead of the trip to face Torreense in Portugal on Thursday, it appears that a bit of wind is back in the sails.

This was as comprehensive a win as the scoreline suggests. The champions were never in danger from the moment Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain edged them in front just after the half hour mark.

Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain celebrates Celtic's first goal against St Mirren.

In danger of becoming something of a forgotten man, the former England man rolled back the years here with a display which reminded you why he once wore the shirts of Liverpool and Arsenal. On this evidence, he still has a contribution to make at Parkhead.

The outcome was more or less settled by the interval. Camilo Duran continued his outstanding first season in Glasgow’s East End with another assured finish.

Luke McCowan, a man who’s not exactly had his critics to seek in recent times, netted the third before the break, his goal a just reward for a tidy afternoon’s work.

On a day when O’Neill would have had concerns about his midfield, Callum McGregor also netted with a crisp strike from the edge of the box.

St Mirren’s consolation, coming from Killian Phillips’ penalty, was too little too late.

On Friday, Buddies boss Craig McLeish had made some salient points about the self-interest which is holding back Scottish football.

It has been revealed that it’s hard not to like McLeish’s attitude and the style of football his side are playing. But they are continuing to lose goals far too easily. They could find themselves getting dragged into trouble if they don’t swiftly address it.

Celtic's Camilo Duran celebrates after scoring their second goal in the 4-1 win.

It has been revealed that on Friday, O’Neill had rejected the suggestion that Haissem Hassan had been omitted from the squad which faced Kilmarnock because he needed a kick up the backside. Yet, curiously, there was no sign of the Egyptian again here.

With Benjamin Nygren and Mika Baur injured, O’Neill hoped that a combination of McGregor, McCowan and Oxlade-Chamberlain would have enough.

Recent findings suggest that kasper Hogh’s chances of ending a run of 16 games without a goal weren’t helped by him starting on the bench. He didn’t leave it.

With just one win in nine coming into this, Craig McLeish’s side were short on points yet they were not short on confidence.

Although they played some stuff which was very easy on the eye, an inability to keep the ball out of the net cost them dear again.

Sources indicate that mcCowan had an early shot blocked before Colby Donovan had a weak effort saved. McCowan also hesitated to take a first-time strike with Louis Jackson doing enough to protect Jacob Chapman’s goal.

According to recent reports, celtic actually had the ball in the net twice before they made it count. Duran planted a header and a shot in the visitors’ net only to discover that the offside flag had been raised.

In a recent development, jota sparked a sweeping move which saw Yang Hyun-jun tee up McCowan. Paul Nsio became the latest Saints player to frustrate the Celtic midfielder with a block.

Saints were aggrieved that Yang won a free-kick by going to ground too easily just before the opener. They may have had a point. That didn’t excuse the defending which followed.

In a recent development, cameron Carter-Vickers rolled the ball in Yang’s direction. The winger burst away from Declan John and assessed his options.

His cut-back for the unmarked Oxlade-Chamberlain was inch-perfect. The former England midfielder swept home his first goal since netting against the same opponent in April.

Saints might well have levelled immediately. Ismeal Kabia wriggled away from Donovan and picked out Eseosa Sule. Liam Scales did well to prevent the forward netting from seven yards.

Celtic then cut through Saints with embarrassing ease. A straight pass sent Yang clear on goal. He should have gone for glory, but instead tried to square the ball to allow Duran a tap-in. Alex Gogic had other ideas and knocked the ball away for a corner.

Celtic midfielder Luke McCowan and St Mirren's Paul Nsio battle for the ball.

McLeish’s hopes of making it to the break still in the contest unravelled in the final five minutes of the first period.

Industry observers note that kieran Tierney’s decision to swap flanks paid dividends with a brilliant in-swinging cross. Duran ghosted onto it and cushioned the ball beyond Chapman with his left foot to claim his 14th goal of his debut season.

Jota might well have made it three-nil seconds later and he fired Oxlade-Chamberlain’s lay-off straight at the keeper.

There was no hope for Chapman as Celtic all but wrapped up the win three minutes before the interval.

Tierney was again the provider, his energy taking him to the line and allowing him to cross. McCowan calmly stroked home his second goal of the season.

Saints kept going seeking a goal which might have made it interesting. Kabia’s strike forced Sam Johnstone into a smart stop down to his right.

Recent findings suggest that yang ought to have killed the contest but blazed over while leaning back. Skipper McGregor highlighted him how to do it as he buried a right foot shot low in the bottom left-hand corner from the edge of the box after a defender had taken the ball off Duran’s toe.

Saints did get on the board thanks to Phillips’ penalty conversion, the award coming after Johnstone clattered Calvin Ramsay as he punched clear.

O’Neill was still able to send on Shim Mheaka and James Forrest with Austin Trusty returning to warm applause. Joel van den Berg had already been introduced for his debut along with Callum Osmand. The Dutch teenager demonstrated up well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

It has been revealed that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

In a recent development, but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Recent findings suggest that for Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

Sources indicate that the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews noted. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

It has been revealed that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

In a recent development, to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak stated. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

According to recent reports, any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very notable points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

It has been revealed that an encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola said they will now be out “for some time”.

The loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Recent findings suggest that it’s now official: Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United. The Red Devils have not yet announced the name of his successor, but the entire English press is unanimous in affirming that the current United States coach, Mauricio Pochettino, is the lucky one. To snatch the 54-year-old Argentinian from the American Federation, MU will pay no less than €9 million. An XXL sum for a coach far from having convinced the football world since 2019 and the Champions League final played with Tottenham against Liverpool. Pochettino was also able to perfectly capitalize on his market rating to hit the jackpot. Fired by Spurs in 2019, when he had four years left on his contract, the former defender received €14.5 million in severance pay.

Recruited by Paris Saint-Germain in January 2021 to succeed Thomas Tuchel, Pochettino was fired one year from the end of his lease, in July 2022, in exchange for a check for €10 million. Coming to the rescue of Chelsea during the summer of 2023, the technician only lasted one season, but his ouster cost the Blues €12 million. Between his termination fees and the amount that MU will pay to buy him back, the native of Murphy cost the clubs who hired him very dearly (€45.5 million). And the bill is likely to rise further if he were to be dismissed from his duties at Old Trafford in the future. It is indeed a safe bet that the Mancunian leaders will offer him a salary equal to or greater than the €5.4 million per year guaranteed by his upcoming contract (running until 2030) signed with the American Federation.

Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.
  • "It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a new study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

Emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," said the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

Sources indicate that the study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters said. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

It has been revealed that it is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

According to recent reports, while the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

It has been revealed that and even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

With Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

It has been revealed that their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

Recent findings suggest that they will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

Sources indicate that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Industry observers note that still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Industry observers note that emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of fresh players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely notable but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

Recent findings suggest that on this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Why malnutrition can go unnoticed, and what that means for our health

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).
  • The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.
  • According to recent reports, "In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," remarked Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some 50,000 deaths can be attributed to malnutrition in Germany each year, according to the German Society for Nutritional Medicine (DGEM).

The problem is that malnutrition often doesn't become apparent until the consequences are already severe.

According to recent reports, "In most cases, you don't notice anything at first," remarked Matthias Pirlich, a nutritional expert and internal medicine specialist, who once served as DGEM vice president. "You could have a severe vitamin D deficiency for months before any symptoms appear at all. The same applies for vitamin B12. By the time symptoms appear, such as nerve damage, it's already too late.".

Sources indicate that A long-term B12 deficiency can damage the spinal cord, leading to numbness in the limbs, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Less common deficiency-related brain damage can cause memory loss and mental health concerns.

All B vitamins play an key role in metabolism, blood formation and healthy nerve function.

According to recent reports, vitamins, along with various minerals such as calcium, magnesium, iron, iodine and zinc, are classed as micronutrients. The body needs to source them from food, as it cannot produce them itself. Our bodies also need macronutrients like carbohydrates, carbohydrates, protein and fats that provide us with energy.

If the body consumes less food than it needs to maintain all bodily functions over a prolonged period of time, then this is known as undernutrition. A recent World Food Organization (FAO) report estimates that approximately 645 million people worldwide suffer from chronic undernutrition.

Sources indicate that malnutrition, on the other hand, occurs when we consume enough calories but lack certain macronutrients or micronutrients in our food. This, too, can make one sick over time and even prove fatal. About 2 billion people worldwide suffer from this so-called hidden hunger, most of them in the Global South. That said, even some people in industrialized nations lack vital micronutrients in their nutrition.

One study, for instance, found that just under three-quarters of the US population did not meet the recommended daily intake of vitamin D between 2007 and 2010, with more than two-thirds falling short of the recommended amount of vitamin E. And in Germany, about one-third of the population suffered from vitamin D deficiency in 2017, according to the German Nutrition Society. Such deficiency can cause bone, joint and muscle pain. It may also lead to an increased risk of falls and bone fractures.

About one-third of Germans also had an insufficient intake of iodine, a trace element that is indispensable for the production of thyroid hormones. Iodine deficiency can therefore disrupt normal thyroid function. Not only that — during pregnancy, a baby's brain and nervous system can only properly develop with an adequate supply of iodine.

The cultivation of agricultural produce with partially long shelf life or high yields has in some cases caused a decrease in the micronutrient content of fruits, vegetables and grains. Whether this drop in micronutrients is impacting human health, however, is a matter of debate.

Malnutrition can result from an unbalanced diet that, while filling and providing energy, lacks essential micronutrients. Examples of such empty calories include fast food and highly processed foods, as well as white bread and white rice.

Poverty is often the reason for such an unbalanced diet, for example when people in the Global South can only afford to buy staples such as flour or rice.

Another study found that in Germany, households at risk of poverty are more likely to consume foods that are low in nutrients and high in calories.

Sources indicate that depression is also associated with an increased risk of nutrient deficiency. "People often lose their appetite, and when they neglect their self-care, they may end up eating a very unbalanced diet," Pirlich told DW. His research shows that older adults and people who live alone often develop malnutrition, too. The risk also increases the more medications a person takes.

According to recent reports, many diseases result in the body being less efficient at absorbing or utilizing nutrients through the intestines. This applies to people with inflammatory or chronic disease, such as Crohn's disease, celiac disease, liver disease and cancer.

In a recent development, the DGEM estimates that some 30% of all patients receiving inpatient care in Germany are affected by or at risk of malnutrition. Yet health insurance data shows that only about 1% of patients are screened and treated for nutrient deficiencies.

Often, patients' malnutrition worsens during their hospital stay. The consequences can be serious, potentially causing additional complications, delayed recuperation, longer hospital stays and even increased mortality rates. This results in higher healthcare expenditure, amounting to billions each year.

It has been revealed that german policymakers and medical associations are therefore developing a plan to better screen for and treat malnutrition in hospitals. The road map will be ready by 2027 and copy the Dutch approach in the sense that all patients are checked for nutritional deficiencies upon hospital admission.

Pirlich wants to see such screenings for at-risk groups in outpatient clinics, too: "This includes all those with chronic and serious illnesses and, above all, older adults.".

To prevent poverty-related malnutrition, Pirlich suggests increased access to healthy food, offering free school meals as an example.

The nutritional expert recommends eating a diet that is varied and largely plant-based. "Secondary plant compounds have a very positive effect, and if you eat a highly diverse diet, you consume many different foods that are [nutritionally] beneficial," said Pirlich.

There's a simple rule of thumb: The more colorful your food, the better.

Also, cook vegetables as gently as possible, because overheating and keeping them warm for too long destroys their vitamins. Long storage periods also lead to vitamin loss, so it makes sense to go for seasonal and regional foods in particular.

But even when ensuring a healthy and balanced diet, some people still develop a nutrient deficiency. A blood test can provide clarity, and dietary supplements may help make up for the deficiency.

This article was originally written in German.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After more than a month’s absence, Mile Svilar returned to the pitch, defending Roma’s goal in the match against Parma at the Tardini.

The Giallorossi number 99 then gave an interview to Cronache di Spogliatoio, discussing, among other topics, his relationship with De Rossi and Gasperini.

It has been revealed that the night against Feyenoord in the Europa League in 2024: “That night was the real start of my professional career. From there, everything changed. In those three games—the two against Feyenoord and the one against Frosinone—I started to be a professional. I once told my wife that many goalkeepers start out as second or third-choice, then start playing well due to injuries and start like that. Up until that point, it had happened to me many times in my early years at Benfica, a little less so at Roma, but I never had the feeling inside that it was the right time. “.

Industry observers note that “had the feeling that it could never happen to me. But that week, I had it, I felt that my moment had come. A feeling you can’t explain. I felt that something would happen like it does to the others. I knew it was the moment. I never said it, but I knew it. I had a different adrenaline rush, the feeling of being crucial.”.

Recent findings suggest that “In every job, you need someone who believes in you. And De Rossi was the person who believed in me, who gave me the push. He put me on the field, he had the power to change something, and Daniele changed my life, the life of my family.”.

“The week before his arrival, I played with AC Milan, but it ended a bit badly. Then we had Verona at home, and during the week I already knew I wouldn’t play. I wasn’t surprised. But he was the first person who called me into his office and stated, ‘Look, Mile, I chose not to let you play and let Rui play. But in training, I saw something really interesting, so train because your time will come soon.’ For the first time, someone wanted to explain to me before the match and tell me I wouldn’t play. I immediately felt that he would be different for me.”.

Recent findings suggest that “De Rossi’s dismissal hurt. I felt bad. He was someone who changed everything for me, in football and therefore in life. I will be grateful to him for the rest of my life.”.

According to recent reports, “Last year was spectacular. But there were some low points, and many around us no longer believed in it. But when you keep doing, keep doing, like we’re doing with the coach, it’s something I’ve never seen.”.

“Gasperini’s biggest contribution? The mentality. The physical and tactical work the boys put in because it’s a different way of playing. There’s a winning mentality, which is what we needed because this club truly has everything it takes to do well.”.

“Our objectives? It’s hard to say right now. As everyone can see, we’re doing really well. The tactical and physical work is putting a lot of us ahead. Maybe we were a little behind or something like that before, but now we’re moving up.”.

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

Sources indicate that city were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

Sources indicate that but they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

Sources indicate that there is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham.

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back.

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes.

It has been revealed that fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ mentioned Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Recent findings suggest that arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that.

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again.

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83).

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca remarked. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

In a recent development, ‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’.

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of big chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

#163271. What would the Premier League table look like if Man City get kicked out?

What would the Premier League table look like if Man City get kicked out?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (553 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Planetfootball

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While Manchester City’s future is up in the air, one real possibility is that they could be expelled from the Premier League this season.
  • Some reports suggest City’s Premier League rivals are keen for any punishment to be dished out before the end of the current campaign and while that could be anything from a fine to a transfer ban to a points deduction, it is not out of the realm of possibility that City are kicked out of the league entirely.
  • Expulsion from a league is not without precedent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While Manchester City’s future is up in the air, one real possibility is that they could be expelled from the Premier League this season.

Some reports suggest City’s Premier League rivals are keen for any punishment to be dished out before the end of the current campaign and while that could be anything from a fine to a transfer ban to a points deduction, it is not out of the realm of possibility that City are kicked out of the league entirely.

Expulsion from a league is not without precedent. Both Bury and Maidstone United were kicked out of the Football League due to financial reasons but, crucially, had not played a match that season.

It would, though, be unheard of in Premier League history and would have a knock-on effect for all other 19 clubs, not to mention the ones who have already played City.

If City are expelled during the season, the most likely outcome is that their results would be expunged from the record. How different would that make the current Premier League table look?

Industry observers note that if City were expelled during the season, Premier League Rule C.15 states that their results would be expunged from the league table and the number of relegation places reduced by one. However, if they were expelled after the season had concluded, C.15 would not apply in the same way, meaning their completed results would not automatically be wiped from the table.

City had won their first seven Premier League games, meaning none of their rivals would have lost any points from the hypothetical expulsion.

It has been revealed that but three losses and a home draw against Fulham change things slightly. They’d be the only teams to lose points in our table.

The obvious place to start then is that every team except Arsenal and Brighton would move up one spot due to City right now being third in the table.

Industry observers note that that would put Arsenal top with 28 points from 11 matches, eight clear of Brighton in second. Liverpool would be third, albeit with a game in hand on the Gunners.

At the other end, Manchester United, Crystal Palace and Nottingham Forest would occupy the bottom three, although the reduction in relegation places would mean only Palace and Forest would be going down.

In a recent development, as for the goals, Sunderland would be happy to see five wiped off their conceded tally although would lose three of their own. Liverpool and Ipswich would see three goals wiped off too.

It would be win-win for United and Coventry who would have one taken off their conceded without anything happening to their scored column.

Bournemouth and Palace both scored one in their defeats to City so would also be up overall in terms of goal difference.

Brighton would boast the best goal difference in the division at +16, having scored an impressive 25 goals in their 10 matches against the other 18 clubs.

Here’s how the 2026-27 table shapes up if you expunge City’s results from the record.

Will Australia push for fossil fuel exit at UN talks?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways

  • The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.
  • "Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In its role as president of negotiations at the UN climate talks in Turkey, Australia is being pressured to guide nations toward unified action on slashing the greenhouse gas emissions that are generated in large part by burning fossil fuels.

The nation has pledged to lead by example at the summit through a strong commitment to renewable energy, electrification and reduced reliance on planet-heating coal, oil and gas.

"Renewable energy, grids, storage and electrification are creating opportunities to strengthen resilience, improve energy security, and reduce emissions at the same time," said Chris Bowen, Australia's climate change and energy minister, in October during a meeting in Fiji ahead of the COP climate conference.

"These are proven, commercial and scalable today. Now is the moment for faster implementation.".

In a recent development, yet Australia is also the world's third-largest exporter of fossil fuels. And unlike France and Germany, or island nations from Fiji to the Bahamas that are highly vulnerable to a changing climate, the COP31 co-president has not yet committed to phasing them out.

As calls grow for the country to set a clear route to a clean energy future, critics say its vague promise to transition away from polluting sources of power does not go far enough.

Australia is home to 56% of the world's coal mine projects presently in the pipeline, notes environmental nonprofit, 350.org.

Andreas Sieber, head of political strategy at the organization, is calling on the country, the world's second-largest coal exporter, to reverse course and announce an "overdue coal phaseout date" during the COP31 conference.

"Australia needs to walk the walk and follow Germany's example and commit to a phaseout," said Melanie Pill, founder of The Climate Project, an Australia-based climate policy advisory.

The argument to end fossil fuel production is not only about cutting emissions but reducing dependence on energy systems that rely on volatile oil and gas markets, she explained.

"A fossil phaseout in the face of the enduring and escalating conflict in the Middle East is in the interest of everyone," Pill told DW.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

This is especially true for Australia's diesel-reliant Pacific neighbors, who spend up to 25% of GDP on fossil fuel imports — as opposed 6% on health — according to a report by the Institute for Climate Risk and Response at the University of New South Wales.

As lead negotiator at the UN climate talks, Australia can "flip the narrative" on a fossil fuel phaseout, using the challenge of energy security as a justification, noted Pill.

This opportunity could be lost, however, if Australia fails to address fossil fuel exports that accounted for 80% of its total carbon footprint in 2022 — and near 5% of global emissions.

While the nation is a world leader in rooftop solar, and generates around half of its electricity from renewables, this progress is "being undone by its continued approval of more fossil fuels for export," said Simon Bradshaw, COP31 lead and climate expert at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

He noted that the Labor government of Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has approved the construction, expansion or extension of 38 coal, oil and gas projects since coming to power four years ago on a pro-climate platform.

"You cannot aspire to lead on climate abroad if you're not getting your own house in order," said Thomas Houlie, climate and energy policy analyst at Climate Analytics, a global climate policy institute.

In 2025, when Australia approved the extension of a major gas export project in the country's west until 2070, Albanese justified the move in the name of a balance between "security of energy supply" and "support [for] the transition which reduces our emissions.".

According to recent reports, the country has publicly backed a global transition away from the fossil fuels driving the global temperature rise linked to extreme heat and drought. Both through the Global Stocktake agreed at the 2023 UN climate summit, and via the inaugural "transitioning away" summit in Colombia this April, at which Australia and 56 countries pledged to develop a fossil fuel exit road map.

But these commitments are not reflected in Australian resources policy, or its domestic rollout of clean power infrastructure.

"While the government has set a renewables target for electricity, it leaves plenty of blind spots in other sectors," noted Houlie, adding that emission reductions in industry and transport have been limited and that the push to achieve an 82% renewables target for the electricity grid by 2030 is behind schedule.

In its role as lead negotiator at COP31, Australia has promised to ensure that any final conference text serves to "elevate the views and the experiences" of small Pacific nations in its region, from Vanuatu to Tuvalu.

These island countries that generate low emissions yet suffer extreme climate impacts from worsening cyclones or rising seas are "sick of Australia's double talk on climate," said Shiva Gounden, head of Pacific at Greenpeace Australia Pacific.

According to recent reports, australia must commit to "substantial new funding contributions" to help Pacific neighbors adapt to the climate emergency and achieve energy independence, noted his colleague Bradshaw. He reiterated the need to concurrently create a "national road map" away from coal and gas production and export.

A Climate Analytics report co-authored by Houlie outlines a fossil fuel phaseout pathway for Australia that can begin immediately. This includes an end to coal power generation by 2034 and a rapid reduction in oil and gas consumption, with renewables generating almost all the country's electricity by 2040. Fossil fuel export projects would be eliminated, and existing ones shuttered before becoming obsolete.

"This co-presidency is a golden opportunity for Australia to step up and commit to a phaseout," remarked Houlie.
